content.text:
Resubmitted with the minimality defect repaired.

**What changed from my prior proposal:** I no longer convert the sentence into a TrueLink-only prohibition. The mutual "Neither party shall assign or transfer ... without the prior written approval of the other party" opener is retained verbatim, so Client's residual consent obligation for assignments outside the carve-out survives — nothing in the preferred checklist required freeing Client to assign to any third party.

**Final redline (validated ok:true, minimality ok):**
1. **Replace inside Section 15** — insert "not to be unreasonably withheld," after the mutual approval requirement, and narrow the exception from "an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate" to "an assignment by Client to an affiliate or successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets." This delivers the Client affiliate and successor carve-outs, keeps TrueLink subject to Client approval (its own affiliate free-pass is removed), and adds the reasonableness standard.
2. **Insert one short sentence** — TrueLink may never assign to a competitor of Client, and a Client change of control gives TrueLink no termination right.

All six preferred elements map exactly once; the fallback's successor-notice mechanic is immaterial because the preferred checklist is fully met. No other mechanic in Sections 13, 14 or 16 is disturbed.
